title: Breaking Free from the Trap of Giving Up on Yourself | David Choe

segments.x: If you want to talk about passive-aggressive, if you want to talk about anger, then look no further than me. Let's talk about me. You know, I've I've prided myself my whole life on getting out while I'm ahead. You know, flirt with disaster, flirt with danger, get right to the line, and then jump right out. And I had

dug myself so deep, I'm almost like incoherent to the point where I can't put a sentence I'm I'm like I was like stuttering and every second that wasn't talking, I was either on my phone or on my laptop. It's not even me. I go, "What? Who is this dark, angry, I feel really like gross." And I

go, "Oh my god, I'm sick." I would do so many things that were against who I was as a person, and I say, "How do I get out of this one?" It was all leading to a very bad place. So, I had to do something very drastic.

And one of the first things that I felt when I went into therapy was that they were brainwashing me. And my therapist looks at me and says, "David, maybe your brain needs to be washed." And I was like, "You're right. I was so dirty and needed to be washed." And as an Asian, mental

health is looked at as not a real disease, and it's looked at as a weakness. It's like, "Just get over it." And most people I I knew that had therapists swore by it. And I said, okay, it's not really looked at as a real thing in Asian culture, but I'll I'll go for it. So, I said, "Okay, I'm

going to go hard." First of all, it's extremely expensive, so most people can't can't afford it, which I have my own issues about. I think mental health care should be free for everyone, and so I'm working on that. I I also feel like the negativity of those words rehab, therapy, mental health, all those things should be

changed into more positive. And so, because I'm a I'm prone to extreme behavior, I felt more like Malcolm McDowell in Clockwork Orange with my eyes peeled back. And so I I dug myself out. I un-brainwashed myself. I dove deep into therapy, rehab, mental health, group therapy, psychodramas, EMDR EMDR eye rapid movement treatment, horse

therapy, dolphin therapy, every form of getting better. If someone said try this, I tried it. And so it was me doing my version. I mean, it's not natural for someone to do therapy 7 days a week for 8 hours a day for 2 years. But that's what I needed because I was at the

bottom. Any sign of morality was gone. And that's I don't have regrets. That was my journey that I had to go through. I needed to reach the bottom so that I could work myself out to the top and live a joyful, happy, fulfilling life. I had to do something very extreme to dig

myself out of that. I did my version of extreme working out. And I worked out my brain and my soul. And now I'm like this mental health creature that's trying to help people. You know, that's one of the scariest things you could ever say to someone. It's like, "Hey, I'm here to help you." I'm really being careful. I'm
really trying to figure out the best way I can help others while helping myself and not becoming a martyr. Like, "Ah, who cares about me? Who cares about my feelings? Who cares about my health?

I'll just throw my into the fire so that everyone else can can eat tonight." I'm tired of the self-destructive behavior. I don't want to enable people. I don't want to enable myself. And I don't need to do that anymore. That's not good for me and that's not good for anyone else.
